verdict.rationale: Rippling's IAM page says dynamic rules handle both account provisioning and group access, keeping access correct as roles change. It also says access, permissions and groups update automatically on role changes or departures, which together replace one-by-one grants. missing for 10: explicit documentation of how dynamic group membership rules are built and how apps are assigned to groups, plus independent or hands-on corroboration beyond marketing pages.

support.subject: As an IT admin, access is assigned by group and rule — dynamic group membership and group-based app assignment replace one-by-one grants

citations.quote: From provisioning accounts to managing group access, dynamic rules automatically ensure the right people get the right level of access—even as their roles change.
When roles changes or someone leaves, Rippling automatically updates access, permissions, and groups.
automatically provisions or revokes access based on role changes, risk signals, and company policy
